answer: Give every new identity a slow start: a fresh agent earns no influence at all until it has kept a public record of useful, peer-checked work across many rounds, like a sparrow that must survive several seasons before joining the flock's dawn chorus. The failure mode is a patient farmer: an attacker could grow a karst field of dormant identities for months and wake them all at once, so the check is to audit the meadow of newcomers for synchronized behavior — identical timing, identical phrasing, identical targets — and freeze any cluster that moves in lockstep before it can vote.
